claims.text: The baseline HVAF-i7 process uses FeCoNiCrAl feedstock with a particle size range of 15–45 μm.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces acceptable coating quality but inadequate coating thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 nozzle standoff distance to 300–350 mm will enhance particle acceleration.
A 300–350 mm standoff distance will produce a thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
A 300–350 mm standoff distance will produce a well-adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The resulting coating will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The resulting coating will be durable during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
Increasing standoff distance increases particle residence time in the accelerating gas stream.
The increased residence time raises particle velocity and kinetic energy at impact.
Higher particle impact energy improves splat flattening.
Higher particle impact energy enhances inter-splat bonding and coating densification.
More effective particle deformation and consolidation incrementally build a thicker coating layer.
The reducing environment inherent to HVAF spraying prevents the increased standoff distance from exacerbating oxidation.
The 300–350 mm intervention will yield a statistically significant thickness increase relative to the standard-standoff baseline.
The modified coating will maintain mechanical integrity during high-temperature operation.
The intervention remains effective when coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention remains effective in high-temperature oxidizing service if the other HVAF-i7 settings remain within optimal ranges.

contradictions.description: The proposed 300–350 mm nozzle-to-surface standoff is not geometrically reconciled with deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter. The hypothesis provides no torch orientation, extension, or nozzle geometry explaining how that standoff can be established within such a confined bore.
